/sprint-x.title: Dhwani Shah
h1: Automated Task Allocation and Sprint Optimization
How might we reduce scrum overload?
h2: Sprint X is a solution to automated task allocation and sprint optimization to streamline agile project management processes.
While Agile frameworks aim to improve efficiency, they can create operational overhead, and routine administrative tasks frequently slow down project reporting and progress tracking.

Sprint X reimagines Agile execution by embedding AI into the core workflow, automatically breaking down complex tasks, generating data driven sprint retrospectives, and eliminating repetitive administrative work, enabling teams to focus on execution rather than process management.
The core of SprintX is the Context-Rich Issue Detail view, primarily designed to eliminate tab-switching.
p: Instead of navigating across tools, specs in a doc, designs in Figma, and code in GitHub, users can access everything they need within a single view.

/about.title: Dhwani Shah
p: I started out as an architect, drawn to designing spaces people would move through, inhabit, and experience. But over time, I realized it wasn’t the finished structure that excited me, it was everything that made it work: the systems, the constraints, the invisible choreography behind the scenes.
Much of my work became about untangling complexity, interpreting ambiguous requirements, balancing competing needs, and designing systems that could actually function in the real world.

When I moved into project management, the pattern became even clearer. Coordinating large infrastructure and data center projects, I encountered inefficiencies at every turn. So I started designing solutions: automating processes, building tracking systems, and smoothing the flow of information across teams. That’s when it clicked - I realized I wasn’t just drawn to structures or projects. I was drawn to designing systems themselves.
Product design felt like the natural next step.
It built on everything I already cared about: understanding people, working within constraints, collaborating across teams, but with speed, iteration, and immediate impact.

Today, I approach product design the way I approached architecture: starting with the user, designing systems around real needs, and obsessing over how things work in practice. My background still shapes my thinking: balancing form and function, noticing the small details that make a system feel seamless, and making sure every design actually functions.

I’m particularly drawn to workflow-heavy products/tools people rely on daily but often struggle with because they’re fragmented, inefficient, or unintuitive. Projects like Tally, an AI-Native bookkeeping tool for freelancers, and Sprint X, a system for streamlining team planning, come straight from problems I’ve faced myself, usually where my best ideas start.
I’m especially interested in building at the intersection of AI and workflow automation; spaces where friction is still high, and thoughtful design can genuinely transform how people work.

/tally.title: Dhwani Shah
h1: Upload receipts, AI does the rest
How might we streamline expense tracking and organization for freelancers and startups so it requires minimal time and effort?
h2: Tally is an AI-Native receipts-to-bookkeeping agent for automating end-to-end expense tracking, receipt extraction, categorization, and filing.

Administrative tasks like logging receipts and updating spreadsheets steal valuable hours that could be spent on billable work. Freelancers and small business owners manage multiple responsibilities like client delivery, operations, communication, and finance. Within these competing priorities, capturing and tracking small expenses is often delayed or overlooked.

Tally began as an exploration into making financial tracking feel less like traditional bookkeeping and more like a seamless part of daily workflows. Instead of building a full accounting platform, it focuses on a lightweight system that enables independent professionals to quickly capture expenses, organize them by project, and maintain real-time visibility into spending. By automating expense tracking for freelancers and small businesses, Tally eliminates manual data entry. Users can simply upload a receipt image or send a message, and AI extracts, organizes, and securely records the expense in real time.

/curalink.title: Dhwani Shah
h1: An Integrated Approach to Revolutionizing Medication Management and Access
What happens when care moves beyond the clinic?
Digital health is projected to cross $1T by 2034
People can access care more easily, but navigating it is still confusing
How might we enhance medication access, communication, and adherence through a connected, user-centered experience?
h2: This case study showcases how I balanced technological solutions to address the fragmented medication management system, undertaken as a solo bootcamp project. Discover the strategic user research and design conceptualization behind CuraLink, an app designed to empower patients through real-time pharmacy data, AI-driven adherence support, and streamlined healthcare communication.

As the solo designer for CuraLink, my role involved an 8-week research and a 4-week prototyping phase. My responsibilities encompassed user research, system design, prototyping, illustration, user flow creation, and storytelling. Utilizing Miro, Figma, and Photoshop, my responsibilities often blended with product ownership and business analysis, ensuring CuraLink's desirability, viability, and technical feasibility
Medication access and adherence is fragmented due to outdated tech and poor patient-pharmacy-provider connectivity.

Telehealth now accounts for ~40% of digital health, evolving into a core layer of care as the broader market moves toward a $1T future. Health management is no longer episodic, it happens in real time, integrated into everyday life.

Telehealth now accounts for ~40% of digital health, evolving into a core layer of care as the broader market moves toward a $1T future. Health management is no longer episodic, it happens in real time, integrated into everyday life

Healthcare today spans providers, pharmacies, devices, and caregivers, but these systems rarely work together. As a result, users are left to navigate complexity on their own, turning care into a fragmented and overwhelming experience.

While technology is expanding access, it often fails to support how people actually live with their health. Especially for older adults, poorly designed systems create friction, reducing confidence, independence, and the overall sense of care.
Streamline medication management, strengthen patient-pharmacy-provider connectivity, and empower users with real time insights to improve adherence and access.

CuraLink enables structured tracking of medication adherence and health metrics through a streamlined logging interface. The system uses AI-based predictive algorithms to forecast refill needs based on dosage schedules and historical intake, prompting timely user actions. Real-time pharmacy integration pulls live inventory and dynamic pricing data via API from partnered networks, allowing location-based, cost-optimized medication access.
